result: In 24 CDC-criteria CFS patients vs 21 sedentary controls, resting TGF-beta appeared higher (median 43.9 vs 18.9 ng/ml, P=0.003) but this was traced to assay-batch variation; no other cytokine protein or RNA differed and exercise or commuting did not change cytokines.
reason: Independent cohort showing the TGF-beta elevation is artefactual, but via assay batch rather than the centrifugation/platelet mechanism the finding describes, so it extends rather than replicates.

result: A survey of 1428 patients, compared with secondary surveys totalling 16,665, found CBT helped 8-35%, GET caused negative responses in 54-74%, and pacing was most favoured, with 44-82% reporting benefit.
reason: The paper does not test the Eckey severity or cluster claims; it does replicate pacing as the top-rated approach in patient surveys.

result: A survey of 1428 patients, compared with secondary surveys totalling 16,665, found GET caused negative responses in 54-74%, CBT helped only 8-35%, and pacing had the lowest negative response rate.
reason: Independent patient-survey data showing frequent worsening after GET, the same direction as the finding.

result: A review of CBT studies that used objective outcomes found no evidence that CBT improves physical capability or objective measures such as return to work.
reason: Extends the PACE point that self-report gains are not matched by objective measures to the wider CBT literature.

result: In 48 CFS, 19 MS and 30 healthy controls, CFS had 25% lower finger pressure pain thresholds and higher finger temporal summation than MS, but conditioned pain modulation did not differ at either site and differences from healthy controls were smaller than those between the patient groups.
reason: It tests CPM and finds no impairment, against the finding's claim of impaired CPM; the hyperalgesia differences are mainly against MS, not against healthy controls, so the evidence is mixed.

result: A 51-plex CSF cytokine assay in 32 classical and 27 atypical ME/CFS cases found lower IL-17A and CXCL9 in atypical cases, sparser cytokine networks, and an IL-1RA pattern in classical cases suggesting disturbed IL-1 signalling.
reason: Same assay and group as Hornig 2015, adding a subgroup comparison and support for IL-1 disturbance; there are no healthy controls and the classical cases likely overlap.

result: A 51-plex CSF cytokine assay in 32 classical and 27 atypical ME/CFS cases found distinct profiles, with lower IL-17A and CXCL9 in atypical cases and an IL-1RA-centred network in classical cases.
reason: Adds a phenotype-defined CSF immunotype split; small, patient-only comparison with no replication.

result: In CCC-defined CFS/ME patients from a primary care clinic, serum activin B was raised against controls and the reference interval, while activin A, follistatin, routine pathology and IL-2/4/6/10/17A, TNF and IFN-gamma were normal.
reason: The atlas has an activin B finding (muscle-exertion-activin-b); its claim text was not in the index, so the relation is set to extends pending a check that it is not already cited.

result: Complete mtDNA sequencing of 93 UK and South African CFS patients found none of the more than 200 clinically proven pathogenic mtDNA mutations.
reason: It tests pathogenic mtDNA mutations, not haplogroups or common SNPs, and explicitly leaves population variants open; no atlas finding covers pathogenic mtDNA mutations.

result: In 60 adolescents with CFS, 31 with asthma and 78 healthy, baseline RMSSD was lower in CFS and asthma than in healthy controls; during recovery from a social stress task, the CFS group showed no HRV recovery and a continued rise in skin conductance.
reason: Independent adolescent cohort with lower resting vagal HRV (RMSSD); the asthma group was also lower, which fits the finding's note that the change is non-specific.
